catalogTopics.method: Question-content review against current CED; scanned page checked

candidates.name: Coulomb's law and effective nuclear charge
candidates.definition: Explaining atomic and ionic behavior through the electrostatic attraction between charges, which grows with charge magnitude and shrinks with distance, including shielding and effective nuclear charge.
candidates.include: Tag when the explanation must invoke charge magnitude, distance, shielding or effective nuclear charge to justify a trend or comparison.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag lattice-energy comparisons already tagged lattice-energy unless the reasoning is explicitly about Coulomb's law at the atomic level; do not tag simple recall of a trend direction.

candidates.name: Atomic and ionic radius
candidates.definition: Predicting and explaining the sizes of atoms and ions across periods and down groups, including isoelectronic ions and ions versus their parent atoms.
candidates.include: Tag when atomic or ionic size is compared, ranked or explained.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when ion size is only one input to a lattice-energy argument unless the size comparison itself is asked.

candidates.name: Ionization energy
candidates.definition: Trends in first ionization energy and the pattern of successive ionization energies, including using large jumps to identify valence electrons.
candidates.include: Tag when first or successive ionization energies are compared, ranked, explained or used to identify an element or group.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag PES questions unless ionization energy itself is compared outside the spectrum.

candidates.name: Electronegativity trends
candidates.definition: The tendency of an atom in a bond to attract shared electrons, its periodic trend, and its explanation from nuclear charge and distance.
candidates.include: Tag when electronegativity values or trends must be compared or explained as the main reasoning.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when electronegativity is only used to decide bond polarity (tag bond-polarity) or acid strength (tag acid-strength-structure).

candidates.name: Electron configurations and atomic structure
candidates.definition: Subatomic particles, isotopes and ion charge, and writing or interpreting ground-state electron configurations of atoms and ions using the Aufbau principle, Hund's rule and the Pauli principle.
candidates.include: Tag when the student writes, reads or uses an electron configuration, identifies core versus valence electrons, or counts protons, neutrons and electrons.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag when the configuration is only implied by a periodic-trend explanation that already rests on Coulombic attraction; Aufbau exceptions and quantum-number assignments are not assessed.

candidates.name: Integrated rate laws and half-life
candidates.definition: Using concentration-versus-time relationships for zero, first and second order reactions, linear plots ([A], ln[A], 1/[A] versus time), rate constants from slopes, and first-order half-life.
candidates.include: Tag when concentration at a time, half-life, or order from a linear plot must be determined.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag initial-rate tables (tag rate-law).

candidates.name: Rate laws and reaction order
candidates.definition: Determining reaction orders, the overall order, the rate constant and its units from experimental data, typically initial rates, and predicting rate changes when concentrations change.
candidates.include: Tag when orders, a rate law, k, or a predicted rate change must be determined.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag mechanism-based rate-law derivation (tag mechanism-rate-law) or integrated-rate-law graphs (tag integrated-rate-laws).

candidates.name: Bond polarity and partial charges
candidates.definition: Using electronegativity difference to decide whether a bond is polar, the direction of its dipole, and which atom carries the partial negative charge.
candidates.include: Tag when bond dipoles or partial charges on bonded atoms must be identified or compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag whole-molecule polarity questions unless individual bond dipoles are explicitly reasoned about (tag molecular-polarity).

candidates.name: Photoelectron spectroscopy (PES)
candidates.definition: Reading PES spectra: peak position as binding energy of a subshell, relative peak height as number of electrons, and connecting spectra to electron configuration and nuclear charge.
candidates.include: Tag when a PES spectrum is given, sketched or predicted, or binding energies of subshells are compared.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag ionization-energy trend questions that never refer to subshell binding energies or spectra.

candidates.name: Ionic solids and lattice attraction
candidates.definition: The structure of ionic solids as lattices of alternating cations and anions, and comparing the strength of lattice attraction from ion charge and ion size.
candidates.include: Tag when ionic compounds are compared by melting point, lattice energy or hardness using ion charge and radius, or the lattice structure is described.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag classification of a solid as ionic without a lattice-strength argument (tag solid-types).
